title: What If 3 Billion Passenger Pigeons Still Darkened the Sky?

scenes.text: What if the most common bird in North America hadn't died out? There were billions of them.
Estimates say three to five billion passenger pigeons lived here, up to 40 percent of all the continent's birds.
In 1813, Audubon counted 163 flocks in 21 minutes, and they kept passing for three days.
They flew up to 60 miles an hour, and one nesting colony in Wisconsin once covered 850 square miles.
Then came hunting, and cleared forests. The last wild one was shot in 1910.
The last of them, a bird named Martha, died in a Cincinnati zoo on September 1, 1914.

description:
What if the passenger pigeon never went extinct?
Three to five billion birds once filled North American skies, and Audubon watched one flight for three days.
